chapter: Mario Bauza and the Cuban sextets
title: Why Afro-Cuban families chose music
summary: Machito says music was a way out, comparing black entertainers in the US before publishers and white bands took control.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Macho, I've been learning a lot that most Cuban families, or Afro-Cuban families like the Socarras family, almost everyone in the entire family was in music. Why did they select music?
Well, let me tell you. Ah - we had a - even an entire black family had a great European influence because Spain, we were very lucky to practically, but maybe

other people had a different opinion, to be discovered by Spanish. We were the best friend, the sweetheart of Spain; like when Spain lost Cuba, America, the United States, fall in love with Cuba. We had from the United States everything. Now you could see what is going on.

But, what I am driving at is that I notice that in the United States becoming a boxer or a basketball player or a baseball player, seems to be the way out of the ghetto. Was it the same thing over there? Music for the Afro-Cuban? Was this a chance for you to rise to a better status?

In those days, like in the United States thirty, forty, fifty years ago, the black musician was what - the power in the entertainment field; comedian, dancers, so forth, so on; so the way out to has some - bring some bread and butter to the house is to be a tap dancer like Bill Robinson and ah - Bill Bailey, and the other guy, the other guy, the Nicholas Brothers, the other guy and the other guy, so, Duke Ellington, Count Basie, Fletcher Henderson, you name it. They was the one to have control of the music until the publishing company got wise and in those days we had discrimination in the United States, so they were limited. The The record selling, the - a million things, so that was when became ah - eh - Benny Goodman and Artie Shaw and Tommy Dorsey, and the other guy and the other guy; but before who had control of the entertainment, dance, dancing entertainment, was a black, black orchestra, Calloway and the rest.
I see. Okay, so then one of the reasons why Afro-Cubans families went for music was probably because it was a way to earn a livelihood and recognition.
